doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Blue Note, The Connection and Tony Williams
title: Tony's concept of time and Jack DeJohnette
summary: McLean admired Tony's open time, then replaced him with Jack DeJohnette.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What did Tony bring to the table that was different or revolutionary?

I think I just liked the energy that he used and his concept of time, how he didn’t use the 2-4 on the sock cymbal all the time, just playing [McLean claps on 2 and 4], like that. I just liked his concept. It was more open, and found that he was open to doing a lot of interesting things musically that I was interested in.
Did you see him and Jack DeJohnette as similar in that?

They’re both young drummers that are thinking about some other ways to play the rhythm. So when I – when he went with Miles, I called Jack immediately. Had a rehearsal the next day. And he was bam, right there, in the band.
So were you, like, training drummers for Miles?
Nah. It seems like that, doesn’t it? Yeah. It seems like that.
Because, did you tell Jack DeJohnette that he would be Miles’s next drummer?
No, I didn’t say – I didn’t know nothing about that.
Somebody had construed a quote along those lines. Somewhere I picked it up.
I don’t think so. I don’t remember that.
